crisis.check: I want to check in, because what you said matters. If someone is hurting you, or you're thinking of hurting yourself or not wanting to live, please don't carry this alone.
crisis.support: What you said matters to me, and I care about you. I can't replace a person being with you right now. If you're in danger, call an ambulance on 997 or go to the nearest emergency room, or call the Ministry of Health on 937. If you can, reach out to someone you trust right now.

rules.understood: Sounds like you've got a lot going on today. Here's what I understood: {{facts}}. Should I save that to shape today's mission? That's only from what you said, and I'm not guessing beyond it.
rules.noResults: I don't have any records yet. Once you finish a mission, I can tell you about your actual results.
rules.results: You have {{total}} attempts on record and completed {{done}}{{avg}}. This is just for your own tracking and doesn't measure your health.
rules.greet: Hey there! I'm doing well. How about you? How's your sleep and your day?
rules.thanks: You're welcome! I'm here if you need me, and don't forget time with the people you love.
rules.fallback: I hear you. Want to tell me more about your day? If you'd like to try something light, you can start today's mission from Home.

advice.prioritize: That's a lot to fit around a full day. One way in: pick the one thing that matters most tonight, give it a short, fixed slot, and treat the rest as optional. Your other interests can each get their own evening in the week. If you like, the activity below helps you sort what comes first.
advice.start: Starting is often the hardest part. Shrink the first step until it feels almost too easy, like opening the file or writing one line, and give it two minutes. Once you've started, carrying on is easier.
advice.focus: For focus, one thing at a time helps: put your phone out of reach, choose one small piece of the material, and work in a short block with a break after. Short and finished beats long and scattered.
advice.stress: Sounds like a heavy day. It's fine to pause before anything else: a few slow breaths, some water or a short walk. There's a short, optional break below if you'd like it.
advice.sleep: Winding down works best as a routine: dim the lights, put screens away a little before bed, and do something slow and calm. If trouble sleeping goes on for weeks, it's worth talking to a doctor.
advice.worry: When thoughts keep circling, it can help to split them in two: what you can do something about, and what you can't. For the first, pick one small next step. For the second, it's okay to set it down for now.
advice.social: Feeling nervous before speaking up is really common. Preparing one or two points, and especially your first sentence, can make starting easier.
advice.rest: Then rest is a perfectly good plan. You don't have to do anything else today. If you want something light later, there's a short break you can try.
advice.memory: Here's a light memory round you can try if you like.
advice.time: If time keeps slipping away, try a timer for each task and notice how long things really take. It makes planning your evening more realistic.

statusAi: Replies come from an AI model (OpenAI) and can be wrong
statusRules: Limited mode: simple rules in the app, not AI. I may miss what you mean.
disclaimer: I'm not a therapist and I don't diagnose. I don't replace your family, friends or professionals.

consent.title: Turn on smart replies?
consent.text: If you agree, your message, recent chat messages and a summary of your challenge results go to OpenAI to produce a reply. We don't send your name or chosen journeys.
consent.note: According to OpenAI's policy, API data isn't used for training and may be kept for up to 30 days to monitor abuse. Don't write sensitive information you don't want to share. You can turn this off any time in My Profile.
